title: Phil Foden, Cole Palmer out of England World Cup squad, Ivan Toney and Kobbie Mainoo in
content:
Manchester City’s Phil Foden and Chelsea’s Cole Palmer have been left out of England’s World Cup squad.

Ivan Toney, who plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, Manchester United’s Kobbie Mainoo, Newcastle United defender Tino Livramento and Arsenal winger Noni Madueke are among the players to have all been selected for this summer’s tournament by head coach Thomas Tuchel, who will name his final 26-man squad on Friday.

Mainoo’s United teammate Luke Shaw has also missed out, along with Chelsea defender Levi Colwill.

Foden, 25, returned to the England squad in November after not being involved in the three previous camps and was again called up in March. He started both of March’s friendlies against Uruguay and Japan.

But Tuchel subsequently cast doubt on his inclusion in the squad for the tournament in the U.S., Canada and Mexico, saying of Foden: “I would say he was excellent in camp but, yeah, he struggles to show it on the pitch.”

Palmer was one of the standout players for England at Euro 2024, scoring in a 2-1 defeat to Spain in the final and helping to turn the semi-final win over the Netherlands from the bench. He was won 14 caps, scoring twice.

Foden has made 49 appearances in all competitions for City this term, providing 10 goals and seven assists, but has again not hit the heights of previous seasons and has played a more restricted role during the final stages of the campaign.

Foden was an unused substitute in both legs of March’s Champions League last-16 defeat to Real Madrid and the FA Cup final win over Chelsea, and played just five minutes from the bench in the crucial Premier League fixture against title rivals Arsenal. He provided two superb assists against Crystal Palace in May, but has not scored since his double against Borussia Dortmund in November.

Foden has been capped 49 times at international level, scoring seven goals. He has been part of the England squad at the past three major tournaments and started all seven matches during his country’s run to the final of the 2024 European Championship.

Toney was not included in the March camp and his last appearance for England came as a brief substitute in the friendly defeat to Senegal on June 10, 2025.

Mainoo’s appearances in England’s March friendlies were his first for the national team since 2024.

Mainoo, 21, was not included in Tuchel’s first three squads of the 2025-26 season, being left out of the September, October and November World Cup qualifiers after falling out of favour with then-Manchester United head coach Ruben Amorim.

Mainoo had informed the club that he was ready to leave on loan that summer after becoming frustrated at his lack of playing time. The 21-year-old started only one game until the new year.

After Michael Carrick’s appointment on January 13, however, the midfielder has seen an upturn in form, starting every game as United secured Champions League qualification for the first time in two years and earning a return to the England squad for their friendlies against Uruguay and Japan.

Mainoo has made 12 senior international appearances in total and was a key part of the 2024 European Championship team that reached the final.

Livramento, who can play on either side of the back four, made his debut in a Nations League win over the Republic of Ireland in November 2024, under interim head coach Lee Carsley, and won the latest of his five caps in the friendly defeat to Japan in March.

The 23-year-old’s season has been disrupted by thigh and hamstring injuries, restricting him to just 17 appearances in the top flight for Newcastle.

Madueke, 24, last played for England in March, appearing as a substitute against Uruguay, before being one of eight players to withdraw ahead of the second friendly against Japan.

Madueke has made 41 appearances for Arsenal during their Premier League-winning campaign but has not started their last three matches after Bukayo Saka’s return to fitness.

In those games — of which, 26 were starts — Madueke has scored seven goals and provided four assists.

Manchester United centre-half Harry Maguire has already revealed he has not made the cut, writing on social media: “I was confident I could of played a major part this summer for my country after the season I’ve had. I’ve been left shocked and gutted by the decision.

“I’ve loved nothing more than putting that shirt on and representing my country over the years.

“I wish the players, all the best this summer”.

England begin the tournament against Croatia on June 17 before facing Ghana on June 23 and rounding off Group L against Panama three days later.

Thomas Tuchel’s squad will travel to the U.S. on June 1, and face New Zealand on June 6 and Costa Rica four days later in warm-up games during their preparation camp in Florida.

Additional reporting by Liam Twomey and Jack Pitt-Brooke
